subject: Tenant hardening — post-demo questions & next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@novumcare.com>, Elena Park <elena@novumcare.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant hardening — post-demo questions & next steps

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-up questions to help us recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). Goal is to validate whether NovumCare needs physical isolation or whether we can meet your SLOs with dedicated capacity + stronger traffic controls.

Top concerns you raised during the demo:
- Noisy neighbor impact during peak inference (esp. model-heavy retrain windows)
- Data residency & encryption-in-flight at edge locations
- Strict latency SLOs for synchronous patient-facing flows (p99 target ~120ms)
- Auditability / retention window for request logs (7 years requested)

A few clarifying asks so we can scope a POC and technical proposal:
1) Typical qps and burst size (avg vs peak). You mentioned 80 qps sustained and 400 qps bursts — can you confirm burst duration?
2) Max tokens per request and average response length (tokens)
3) Do you require provider-managed key separation (HSM/KMS) or will customer-managed KMS be required?
4) Are there procurement / network constraints for opening egress to our hosted regions, or will you prefer a Private VPC appliance?

Proposed next steps:
- Ava to capture a short tenancy-hardening checklist and recommended config choices (attached)
- Quick SE-led architecture call to align on latency SLOs & KV cache strategy (30 min) — propose Monday 04/20 10am PT
- If isolation is required, we’ll prepare a Dedicated capacity proposal + rough pricing; if not, we’ll show a Hosted plan with strict routing & SLA add-ons.

Attachments: redwood-tenant-hardening-checklist.pdf (initial checklist / questions)

Thanks — let me know if the proposed time works and answer the short questions above when you can.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@novumcare.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@novumcare.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 16:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant hardening — post-demo questions & next steps

Diego —

Thanks for the recap, appreciate the clear list. Quick answers inline below and a few extra asks from our side.

1) QPS: The 80 qps is an expected sustained level for Europe/US daytime. Bursts to ~400 qps have happened during marketing pushes; they usually last ~6–10 minutes.
2) Tokens: Typical request payload is ~250 tokens, responses average ~450 tokens. For some clinical summarization flows we’ve seen 1,200 tokens responses (rare).
3) KMS: We need customer-managed keys for model inputs/outputs at rest. We are open to provider-managed for transient caches if encrypted end-to-end, but HSM-backed CMKs are preferred for long-term storage.
4) Network: We want to avoid opening wide public egress from our VPC. If you can support a Private VPC (peered) or an on-prem appliance that is preferable.

Other asks:
- Can you confirm whether request-level logs can be retained for 7 years in encrypted form and exported to our SIEM?
- We will need SOC2 Type II evidence; please attach the most recent report or explain timeline for providing it.

Procurement timeline: evaluating vendors now; procurement expects vendor short-listing by 05/01 and decision in late May.

If Monday 04/20 10am PT works, please send an invite with an agenda (latency, caching, tenancy options).

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
NovumCare

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@novumcare.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant hardening — post-demo questions & next steps

Samir —

Thanks for the details and timeline. Quick technical clarifications (so we size the KV cache and batchers correctly):
- Are the 80 qps measured across all inference routes or only patient-facing models? If across all routes, can you split by route group (auth, triage, summarization)?
- For the 1,200 token responses, is that accounted for in your 6–10 minute burst windows or does it appear independently?
- Is strict data residency only for long-term logs, or must transient in-flight caching also remain within region?

Notes on options:
- Hosted API + Strict routing: We can apply tenant-aware routing (pin NovumCare traffic to reserved worker pools), apply KV prefix caching scoped to your keyspace, and provide per-tenant request throttles. This reduces noisy-neighbor risk but does not provide physical GPU isolation.
- Dedicated capacity: Physical isolation (GPU pool reserved) with SLA uplift. Recommended when you need guaranteed throughput under noisy-neighbor threat or want full control over scaling windows.
- Private VPC / On-prem: Full network isolation, customer-managed KMS, and ability to keep request logs in your VPC — best fit if procurement prevents public egress.

We’ll propose a trial architecture for two paths: (A) Hosted with dedicated reserved worker pools + enhanced throttling (lower cost, faster procurement) and (B) Dedicated capacity proposal (higher cost, stronger isolation).

Attached: redwood-arch-draft.png (initial architecture sketch showing routing & cache boundaries). I’ll update after the call.

Proposed time confirmed: Mon Apr 20 10:00am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Regards,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in procurement context / next steps from the Redwood side. A few things we’ll prepare ahead of the shortlisting deadline (05/01):

- A 2-week Dedicated trial option (pricing + terms draft) so your procurement can evaluate true isolation under load.
- A Hosted-with-reservation plan with exact throttling & KV cache SLAs we can commit to in writing — lower-cost path if that meets your security bar.

Samir — if you can share the procurement contact and any required PO terms, we’ll prepare redlines. Also if you can drop the exact SIEM export format (S3, syslog push, Splunk HEC) we’ll validate retention/export feasibility for 7-year retention.

Diego / Ava — please add the SOC2 PDF and the Dedicated trial T&Cs to the shared drive link Markus will create.

Thanks — looking forward to Monday’s call.

Markus Klein
